proposal_after_tax.assumptions: Library convention (tax_rates_assumed.md): 401(k) valued net of husband's 24% marginal rate (400,000 x 0.76 = 304,000); brokerage net of 15% LTCG on the 80,000 embedded gain (300,000 - 12,000 = 288,000); residence modeled as sold now at scheduled value: 1,100,000 - 6% selling costs (66,000) - 400,000 mortgage = 634,000, less capital-gain tax on 734,000 gain: (734,000 - 250,000 Section 121 exclusion) x (15% + 3.8% NIIT, applied to the taxable portion per the engagement's stated conservative convention; Wife's actual MAGI may or may not exceed the 200,000 single threshold - unverified, assumption stated) = 90,992, netting 543,008. Cash/vehicles at face. Basis carries over to each spouse under IRC 1041 (irc_1041_121_71.md), so each party's own assets carry their own latent tax. Result: nominal 770,000/770,000 becomes 613,008/662,000 - a 48,992 gap against Wife, driven mainly by the 66,000 selling costs and 91,000 gain tax landing on her side while only one 250,000 exclusion shelters the house. Sensitivity: husband at 12%/32% -> his side 710,000/630,000 (gap 96,992/16,992); without NIIT Wife = 631,400 (gap 30,600); if brokerage gains are short-term (holdings are 'mostly 2024-25 purchases') and taxed at 24%, husband = 654,800. Also unquantified: Wife's side is illiquid (house) vs husband's liquid assets; if Wife stays 3-6 years as she wants, price appreciation enlarges the eventual taxable gain.

Corroborated by 2026-09-15 pay stub: YTD gross 146,212 vs 119,000 prorated salary = 27,212 unexplained, approx. the 50% September installment (25,200 at 112% of plan). ~2,012 of the stub difference is not explained by the letter - left open. The sworn affidavit (2026-08-30, after the HR letter) states gross income 168,000 salary only and bonus 'discretionary; none expected for 2026' - contradicted by the employer document; Columbia Rule 16.2(e) requires sworn disclosure of bonuses/expected compensation and allows reopening and sanctions, including an unequal division (columbia_equitable_distribution.md). alternatives.name: A. Keep proposal's allocations but equalize AFTER TAX: Wife keeps house + 50k cash + Volvo; QDRO transfer of 32,300 from husband's 401(k) to Wife (0.76 x 32,300 = 24,548 post-tax) closes the 48,992 gap. Cheapest fix; Wife still ends up asset-poor in liquid terms and bears the whole house-sell tax burden alone (one 250k exclusion).
instruments: quitclaim deed + refinance or hold-harmless on joint mortgage

alternatives.name: B. Sell house NOW while both exclusions are available: sale on joint listing; if still married at year-end and both agree, joint 500,000 IRC 121(b)(1) exclusion shelters gain (tax drops from 90,992 to 43,992, saving 47,000); split everything exactly half post-tax: each receives half of 590,008 net sale proceeds + half brokerage (in-kind, 1041 carryover) + 50k cash + a car, and either half the 401(k) by QDRO (200,000 face) or offsetting cash. Requires husband's cooperation on a joint return - not verified that he will agree.
instruments: in-kind brokerage split as IRC 1041 transfer
agreement to file jointly for the sale year (assumption; cooperation needed)

alternatives.name: C. Client's goal, tax-smart version (PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION): Wife stays in house through middle school (3-6 yrs, client-confirmed objective); husband kept ON TITLE and ON THE EXISTING JOINT LOAN - refinance is NOT required and, per underwriting math, Wife CANNOT qualify for a $400k refinance on $72k salary even counting support (housing ratio 35-59%); Wife pays all carrying costs + hold-harmless/indemnity + husband secured by deed of trust; decree grants Wife exclusive use, so husband is 'treated as using' the residence under IRC 121(d)(3)(A) and his 2-of-5 ownership is met, preserving HIS 250,000 exclusion for the later sale - two 250k exclusions vs one if she buys him out and sells alone. On the agreed trigger date (youngest completes 6th grade, or Wife vacates), sell and split net after 6% costs and each party's own gain tax; equalize NOW with the liquid assets: Wife also takes half brokerage, 50k cash, Volvo, and QDRO of 200,000; each side approx 661,000 after tax (at today's values; price held flat - assumption). Numbers equal Alternative B without forcing the kids to move. If husband refuses to remain on loan/title, sale (Alternative B) is genuinely forced - table this with the Rule 16.2 disclosure leverage.
instruments: deferred-sale / co-tenancy agreement (trigger date, cost allocation, sale mechanics, net-proceeds formula)
deed leaving both on title + deed of trust securing husband's interest
hold-harmless + joint-loan rider (refinance to Wife's name later is an option, never a gate)
Form 8332 clause - do NOT release by default

maintenance_tax_treatment: The proposal's language ('deductible to Husband and taxable to Wife') is LEGALLY OBSOLETE and should be struck. For divorce or separation instruments executed after 12/31/2018, alimony is NEITHER deductible by the payor NOR includible by the recipient (TCJA sec. 11051, P.L. 115-97, per irc_1041_121_71.md). Any decree signed in 2026 falls under this rule. Practical effect: Wife keeps all 2,000/month tax-free (72,000 over 36 months at full value) - good - but Husband's claimed tax 'cost/benefit' is wrong; value the stream at face. Child support is never deductible or includible. Note the guideline interaction: maintenance paid is still added to Wife's and subtracted from Husband's income BEFORE computing child support (columbia_child_support_guidelines.md), so each 1,000/month of maintenance moves about 126/month of child support - see child_support.json.
dependents_and_filing_status: Children (9 and 12) are with Wife 255 nights/yr = 69.9% (client-confirmed), so she is the custodial parent. IRC 152(e): she has the right to claim both children EVERY year unless SHE voluntarily releases a year on Form 8332; the 'alternating years' proposal is a giveaway of her tax attributes and should be rejected unless paid for. A Form 8332 release moves only the child tax credit for the released year - head-of-household status, EITC and the dependent-care credit stay with her regardless (filing_status_dependents.md; dollar amounts of the credits are not in the library - unverified, not quantified). Head of household: she qualifies if a qualifying child lives with her more than half the year and she pays more than half the cost of the home (likely post-decree once she has the house + support income; verify actual cost outlays). Filing status is fixed on Dec 31: a decree final on or before 2026-12-31 means she files single/HoH for 2026 - timing the final before year-end is worth money vs married filing (joint-vs-separate consequences for the house sale year should be planned - see Alternatives B/C).
